tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final configuration on the goal peg must be a descending stack: the largest disk at the bottom and each subsequent disk smaller than the one below it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When checking whether the goal state has been reached or when planning the final placement of disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: For 5 disks, the goal peg should contain [5,4,3,2,1] from bottom to top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free Blocked Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk that has any smaller disks on top cannot be moved directly; those smaller disks must be relocated first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg A has [4,2] (4 bottom, 2 top), move disk 2 elsewhere before moving disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: In a three‑peg problem, the peg that is neither the source nor the destination of a move can serve as a temporary holding place for displaced disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a smaller disk must be moved out of the way of a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: When moving disk 5 from peg B to peg C, use peg A as the auxiliary peg for any intervening smaller disks.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must take the topmost disk from the source peg and place it onto a destination peg whose top disk (if any) is larger, or onto an empty peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing each move in the list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top is disk 2 is illegal because 3 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After writing a complete move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to verify that every move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move sequence, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Step through the moves and confirm that the final peg 2 contains [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The output format expects peg identifiers 0, 1, 2; using any other numbering (e.g., 1‑based) will be rejected.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing each move in the answer list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 from peg 1 to peg 2 is written as [2,1,2], not [2,2,3].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep an up‑to‑date record of the topmost disk on every peg after each move, so you know which disks are movable and which destinations are legal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the construction of the move sequence, after each move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 1 onto peg 0, the top of peg 0 becomes disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Leverage Existing Larger Disks on Target as Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains larger disks that are correctly placed, you can place a smaller disk onto that peg, using the existing larger disks as a stable base.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk has already been positioned on the goal peg and you need to add the next smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 on peg 2, you can place disk 4 onto peg 2 because 5 > 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Destination Peg of Smaller Top Disk Before Placing Larger Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg’s top disk is smaller than the disk you intend to move, you must first relocate that smaller disk (and any disks above it) to the auxiliary peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk onto a peg that currently has a smaller top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Before moving disk 5 onto peg 2, move disk 1 (and then disk 3) off peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Smallest Disk as Flexible Buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be moved onto any peg without violating ordering, making it an ideal temporary buffer; move it repeatedly to free up pegs for larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk is blocked by a smaller disk on the source or destination peg, first relocate the smallest disk to the free peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg A has disk 3 with disk 1 on top, move disk 1 to the empty peg C before moving disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the rule that larger disks cannot be placed on top of smaller ones, especially when focusing on moving a specific disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the size of the moving disk with the top disk of the destination peg; only proceed if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook that only the topmost disk of a peg can be moved, especially when a disk is buried under smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a record of the top disk on each peg and only select that disk for a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to complete the goal peg early by placing small disks before larger ones have been positioned, violating the descending order.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure that any disk placed on the goal peg is either the largest remaining or is being placed on top of a larger correctly positioned disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may default to 1‑based numbering or misinterpret the peg identifiers.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Remember that pegs are numbered 0, 1, 2; double‑check each move’s from‑peg and to‑peg indices before writing them.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the move list is correct without replaying it, leading to unnoticed errors.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After constructing the move list, simulate the entire sequence from the initial configuration and confirm that the final state matches the goal exactly.
